business_problem: TIM needed a fast-data layer that could decouple digital channels from up to 14 legacy back-end databases, support rapid application changes, and sustain performance as the Fly Together modernization program expanded across consumer and business services.
solution_summary: TIM's Fly Together program rebuilt the telecom group's digital experience around microservices and a fast-data layer so customer-facing channels no longer had to query heterogeneous back-end systems directly. After performance tests and architecture analysis, TIM selected MongoDB Enterprise Advanced because the document model could absorb frequent change while still meeting mission-critical scale and robustness requirements. The platform exposes data through APIs to online portals, apps, and ecommerce channels, continuously updating those digital views as source systems change underneath them. MongoDB now acts as the decoupling layer between legacy records and customer interactions, while also supporting operations teams that need traffic and consumption data quickly. TIM says the distributed architecture uses standard, lower-cost hardware, keeps response times almost constant despite higher data volumes, and provides a base for refactoring and a move toward Atlas as-a-service.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Enterprise Advanced
solution_components.role: Provides the fast-data document layer that decouples TIM's digital channels from legacy back-end systems.

data_flow: Changes from up to 14 back-end databases are exposed through APIs into a MongoDB-based fast-data layer. TIM's portals, apps, and ecommerce channels read that continuously updated document model instead of querying source systems directly, and operations teams use the same layer to inspect customer traffic and consumption data quickly.
business_outcome: TIM shortened time to market for new digital services, kept digital-channel response times stable as usage grew, and built a more flexible architecture for omnichannel customer experiences and future cloud expansion.
metrics: TIM is an organization with over 30 million users in Italy and the second largest mobile operator in Brazil.
The system must query up to 14 different databases, all created at different times and based on different technologies.
Fly Together kicked off in 2018 with a focus on TIM's consumer segment; it was extended to include business customers in 2019.
architecture_clues: Fly Together is a microservices-based software infrastructure for TIM's digital channels.
MongoDB serves as the fast-data decoupling layer exposed via APIs rather than replacing every back-end system directly.
TIM's infrastructure is still predominantly on premises, with a future path toward MongoDB Atlas and Google Cloud capabilities.
evidence_quotes: "Fast data means we need a flexible data model, based on a NoSQL database and exposed via API, that continuously updates the data."
"MongoDB Enterprise Advanced was selected over the other alternatives because it met TIM's performance and scalability requirements."
"MongoDB is now the basis of TIM's new 'fast data' structure, helping build the best customer experience for end users."
"MongoDB allows us to respond more rapidly to customer requirements and enables us to change our offering with greater flexibility to provide the best customer experience."
